meaning: Execute verification checks against one unchanged registered graph and matching reconciled plan; report complete requirement accounting without treating unmet runtime-semantic or publication obligations as success.
inputs: Original checked graph and plan; explicit trusted local TypeScript 7.0.2 package root, Node declaration type root, Lean 4.33.1 executable; optional existing whole-project output target. Inert closed options, normalized absolute real paths, and input binding are checked before subprocess execution. No caller check outcomes, callbacks or receipt imports.
checks: source manifest currentness before and after execution
compiled graph obligations and exact graph-plan binding
isolated replay of exact bounded regular source bytes and identical regenerated plan/artifacts
strict native TypeScript compilation of every planned module in one project
independent native TypeScript AST import/export observation against complete planned module inventory
Lean kernel checking, exact standard-foundation axiom audit and full graph/selection round trip
formalization and generated artifact bytes unchanged during checks
read-only exact currentness of an explicitly supplied existing output target
accounting: Include every verification projection requirement exactly once with pass, fail or not_evaluable, causal reasons and evidence for executed checks. Dependencies that fail cannot generate a downstream pass. Add explicitly named Lean check evidence without promoting finite structural proof into full runtime conformance. Any failed check gives fail; otherwise unmet requirements give incomplete; pass requires every requirement satisfied. Current executor leaves selected-generator-semantic-controls, cross-generator-behavior and safe-output-separate-from-planning not_evaluable until their execution/qualification is implemented.
effects: Write only a new private run directory, then clean only that owned directory. Never author source, create or alter a user output target, execute generated domain Operations/Workflows, invoke providers, install tools, fetch dependencies or publish. Source or target drift fails. This is not an OS sandbox for untrusted tool binaries; configured compiler and proof tool installations are a trust boundary.
toolchain: Record native tool versions and relevant package/executable identities. Use argument-vector subprocess calls with bounded output and timeout, remove ambient Node and Lean search-path overrides, construct explicit project configuration without ambient config/plugins, and reject version drift. Do not silently substitute other compilers or observers.
identity: Registered immutable execution report binds the verification input, definition, plan, every result and evidence. Rendering accepts only the in-process report; digest serialization is not proof execution. Local test evidence is not admission or production/runtime authority.
compatibility: Leave existing currentness verify and legacy verify-project behavior unchanged. Stronger CLI wiring remains unfinished while semantic/publication evidence is incomplete; do not expose a pass by bypassing requirements.
